claim: The publication that generated GSE111972 reported CXCR4 among regionally differential and MS-associated genes in human microglia, including high expression in MS normal-appearing grey matter; it did not report the project's exact patient-equal CD44-plus-CXCR4 score or its broad-state adjustment.
future_grounding_route: Treat the publication as same-dataset prior art, not independent replication. Test the frozen CD44/CXCR4 score only in an eligible independent donor-level cohort under docs/validation/MS_MICROGLIA_CD44_CXCR4_REPLICATION_SPEC_V53.md.
project_use: Same-dataset prior-art boundary for the provisional V53 MS microglia association.
relationship_note: This is not independent corroboration because the project reanalyzed GSE111972. It lowers biological novelty for the CXCR4 component while leaving the exact two-gene adjusted analysis as a distinct project computation.

source.citation: van der Poel et al. Transcriptional profiling of human microglia reveals grey-white matter heterogeneity and multiple sclerosis-associated changes. Nature Communications. 2019.
source.label: van der Poel 2019 GSE111972 source publication

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PubMed/Europe PMC bibliographic metadata and short paraphrase
source_terms.reuse_notes: This record stores bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase only; the publication remains external context and shares its data lineage with the project reanalysis.

why_unverifiable: The publication's assertions are external; although the project reran GSE111972 for a different analysis, it did not reproduce every analysis in the source paper.
